title: Trusting WAN Perimeter Security (Missing Transport Encryption)
pattern: Transmitting sensitive or administrative domain payloads in plaintext (HTTP or unencrypted TCP) based on the assumption that the internal subnet or virtual private network is completely secure.
why_bad: The network is not secure [231:231]. Perimeter boundaries are routinely compromised by insider threats, misconfigured firewalls, or lateral movement attacks. Transmitting internal secrets or user PII in the clear enables network sniffer exploits and compromises zero-trust integrity [13:163].
detection: Establishing raw, unencrypted TCP or HTTP connections to endpoints representing separate host instances or subnets [13:163].
fix: Configure Transport Layer Security (mTLS or HTTPS) for all node-to-node and service-to-service communication [13:163].
source: *Building Secure and Reliable Systems* (Adkins), Chapter 5 [13:101]; *Fundamentals of Software Architecture* (Richards & Ford) [21:123].
